# ARCHITECTURE
## Montenegro Weather App — backend-first technical architecture

Status: INITIAL TARGET ARCHITECTURE

This document is the current implementation architecture. It must evolve through recorded decisions in `DECISIONS.md`.

---

# 1. HIGH-LEVEL SYSTEM

```text
                    ZHMS PUBLIC SOURCES
                           |
       +-------------------+--------------------+
       |         |         |        |           |
      AWS    Hydrology   SYNOP   Daily      Forecast/
       |         |         |        |        Sea/Snow
       +-------------------+--------------------+
                           |
                    SOURCE ADAPTERS
                           |
                 FETCH -> PARSE -> VALIDATE
                           |
                      NORMALIZATION
                           |
                      PERSISTENCE
                           |
              DERIVED DATA / FRESHNESS
                           |
                         API
                           |
                     WEB FRONTEND
                           |
                 PWA / later Capacitor
```

The frontend never directly scrapes ZHMS production sources.

---

# 2. INITIAL TECHNOLOGY DIRECTION

Preferred stack:

Backend/runtime:
- Cloudflare Workers

Scheduling:
- Cloudflare Cron

Database:
- Cloudflare D1

Optional raw/debug storage:
- Cloudflare R2

Frontend:
- React + Vite

Source control/shared memory:
- GitHub

CI:
- GitHub Actions

Development:
- cloud-first/browser-first where practical

Packaging later:
- PWA first
- Capacitor later for Android/iOS

---

# 3. WHY THIS SHAPE

The owner has a weak Windows development machine, so cloud-first is preferred.

The project does not need a microservice architecture.

The ingestion workload is periodic and source-specific, making scheduled Worker execution appropriate for the initial design.

D1 is sufficient for structured station/observation/forecast data at the expected scale.

R2 is optional because raw snapshots are useful for debugging, but raw storage is not required for every request.

---

# 4. REPOSITORY SHARED MEMORY

Required repository documentation:

```text
MASTER_SPECIFICATION.md
ZHMS_FORENSIC_EVIDENCE.md
ARCHITECTURE.md
TASKS.md
DECISIONS.md
REVIEW.md
```

Optional:

```text
SOURCE_CONTRACTS.md
TEST_STRATEGY.md
RUNBOOK.md
```

The repo is the persistent project memory across AI providers/chats.

---

# 5. SOURCE ADAPTER LAYER

Recommended shape:

```text
src/
  sources/
    zhms-aws/
    zhms-hydrology/
    zhms-synop/
    zhms-daily/
    zhms-sea-snow/
    zhms-official-forecast/
    zhms-numerical-forecast/
```

Each source adapter should expose a consistent internal contract, conceptually:

```text
fetch()
parse()
validate()
normalize()
getSourceStatus()
```

The exact TypeScript interfaces may evolve during implementation.

---

# 6. COMMON DATA PIPELINE

Every source should fit the following flow:

```text
Source URL
  -> HTTP fetch
  -> content recognition
  -> parser
  -> schema/content validation
  -> normalization
  -> persistence
  -> freshness/status update
  -> derived calculations
  -> API
```

Do not collapse parsing and business logic into one opaque function.

---

# 7. RAW DATA BOUNDARY

Raw source representation should remain an adapter concern.

Internal business logic should consume normalized types.

Example conceptual model:

```ts
interface NormalizedStation {
  stationId: string;
  wmoId?: string;
  name: string;
  latitude: number;
  longitude: number;
  elevation?: number;
  stationType?: string;
  sourceStatus?: number | boolean | string;
}

interface NormalizedObservation {
  stationId: string;
  measuredAt: string;
  fetchedAt: string;
  temperatureC?: number;
  precipitationMm?: number;
  windSpeedMs?: number;
  windDirectionCode?: number;
  windDirectionDeg?: number;
  gustMs?: number;
  humidityPct?: number;
  pressureHpa?: number;
  insolationWm2?: number;
}
```

The exact production schema must be tested and adjusted to real source behavior.

Never fabricate fields when the source does not provide them.

---

# 8. FETCH LAYER RULES

Use GET.

Do not depend on HEAD because forensic testing showed frequent 403 behavior.

Keep TLS verification enabled.

Use a clear, consistent User-Agent where appropriate.

Control request pacing.

Prefer one bulk source request over dozens of station-by-station requests when the public source already provides bulk data.

Avoid duplicate requests across features.

---

# 9. VALIDATION LAYER

Validation should cover:
- expected content shape;
- expected variable names;
- required station identifiers;
- timestamp syntax;
- numeric parseability;
- reasonable numeric ranges;
- missing/empty values;
- schema changes;
- unexpected response type.

A successful HTTP status is not sufficient.

---

# 10. PREVIOUS-KNOWN-GOOD

Important source state should support:

```text
last_valid_payload
last_successful_sync
last_error
source_status
```

When a new payload fails validation:

```text
reject new payload
keep last valid state
record error
mark source degraded/stale
```

Do not destroy useful data because a single fetch was malformed.

---

# 11. FRESHNESS MODEL

Store at least:
- source measurement timestamp;
- backend fetched timestamp;
- last successful synchronization time.

Where publication time cannot be observed, do not invent it.

Freshness should be computed from measurement timestamp where appropriate, but API responses should expose enough metadata for the frontend to tell users whether data is current or stale.

---

# 12. CURRENT EXTREMES ARCHITECTURE

Current extremes are a derived read-model/business function.

Pipeline:

```text
Current normalized observations
             |
      determine reference
             |
      apply <= 2h eligibility
             |
   exclude invalid/ineligible
             |
         aggregate
             |
        current extremes
```

Do not initiate new upstream requests solely for this calculation.

Potential API:

`GET /api/stations/extremes`

Alternative naming such as `/api/temperature-extremes` is acceptable only if it remains consistent with the broader requirement that wind and precipitation extremes are also included.

---

# 13. DATABASE DIRECTION

D1 should store normalized structured data.

Likely logical tables/entities:

```text
stations
station_observations
station_timeseries
hydrology_stations
hydrology_observations
sea_observations
snow_observations
forecasts
source_sync_status
current_extremes_cache (optional derived cache)
```

Exact schema is to be designed task-by-task after the real source contracts are implemented.

Do not create twenty tables merely because the source has twenty arrays.

Normalize for application behavior, not raw-source imitation.

---

# 14. TIME-SERIES STORAGE

AWS graphs expose timestamp/value series grouped by parameter.

A normalized design should make parameter/time lookup efficient.

Possible representation:

```text
station_timeseries(
  station_id,
  measured_at,
  parameter,
  value
)
```

Whether a wide or long schema is ultimately chosen should be decided during implementation based on query patterns and D1 simplicity.

---

# 15. API LAYER

Potential API surface:

```text
GET /api/stations
GET /api/stations/:id
GET /api/stations/:id/observations
GET /api/stations/:id/timeseries
GET /api/stations/extremes
GET /api/sea
GET /api/snow
GET /api/forecast/official
GET /api/forecast/numerical
GET /api/status
```

The final API contract should be documented once implemented.

The frontend consumes these normalized endpoints.

---

# 16. SCHEDULER

There is no universal refresh schedule.

Initial architecture should allow source-specific schedules, for example conceptually:

```text
AWS current       -> frequent polling
AWS graph         -> aligned to actual need/source cadence
Hydrology         -> source-aware schedule
Sea/Snow          -> term/source-aware schedule
SYNOP             -> independent schedule
Forecast          -> metadata/cache-aware schedule
```

Exact cron design should be derived from additional controlled observation and cost/load considerations.

---

# 17. ADAPTIVE SCHEDULING PRINCIPLE

The scheduler should eventually incorporate observed source behavior.

Do not assume:

`all data changes every N minutes`.

Instead:
- poll high-value current source appropriately;
- detect whether new observations are appearing;
- avoid unnecessary repeated heavy downloads;
- use conditional GET where supported for static resources.

---

# 18. FORECAST CACHING

Static numerical forecast HTML resources expose Last-Modified/ETag-type cache metadata in observed tests.

Use conditional retrieval where it is reliable and useful.

Do not depend on HEAD.

Re-test actual 304 semantics during implementation for each relevant resource family.

---

# 19. ERROR HANDLING

Errors must have at least three conceptual classes:

1. transport error
2. parse/validation error
3. stale/degraded source state

Examples:
- timeout;
- TLS failure;
- 404/403;
- 200 + unexpected content;
- 200 + empty payload;
- schema mismatch.

They should not all look like “no data”.

---

# 20. OBSERVABILITY

Record enough information to answer:
- when was the source last fetched?
- did fetch succeed?
- did parse succeed?
- did validation succeed?
- when was the last valid observation time?
- how many stations were accepted?
- how many were stale?
- was schema changed?

A source status endpoint should eventually expose operational health without exposing internal secrets.

---

# 21. TESTING STRATEGY

Tests should exist at several levels:

### Unit tests
- parsers;
- field mapping;
- timestamp parsing;
- wind code conversion;
- freshness;
- current extremes.

### Contract/fixture tests
- known captured ZHMS responses;
- schema changes;
- empty responses;
- `no data` responses.

### Integration tests
- source adapter -> normalization -> storage.

### API tests
- endpoint shape;
- unavailable states;
- stale metadata;
- current extremes.

---

# 22. SECURITY

Minimum rules:
- no TLS bypass;
- no secrets committed to Git;
- use environment bindings/secrets appropriately;
- validate source content;
- sanitize any source-derived strings before frontend rendering;
- do not trust upstream HTML as safe arbitrary application content;
- keep admin/debug routes protected or absent.

---

# 23. FRONTEND BOUNDARY

Frontend should never become the ZHMS scraper.

Good:

`Frontend -> App API -> Normalized DB/cache`

Bad:

`Frontend -> meteo.co.me -> scrape/parse in browser`

The backend is responsible for stable source integration.

---

# 24. FUTURE MOBILE PACKAGING

PWA is the first target.

Once web behavior is stable:

`React/Vite web app -> Capacitor -> Android/iOS`

Native packaging must not force a second backend architecture.

---

# 25. ARCHITECTURE CHANGE RULE

Any significant change must be:
1. proposed;
2. explained to owner in beginner-friendly terms;
3. recorded in `DECISIONS.md`;
4. reflected here;
5. reflected in tasks if implementation work changes.

No silent architecture drift.

# DECISIONS
## Montenegro Weather App — durable project decisions

Rule: this file records WHY the project chose a direction. New AIs must read it before proposing a contradictory architecture.

Status: ACTIVE

---

# DEC-001 — Backend-first before final frontend design

Decision:
Stabilize the backend/data layer before producing the final frontend design specification.

Why:
The UI depends on real source contracts, freshness semantics, normalized data, and API behavior. Designing the final frontend too early risks building UI around assumptions.

Consequence:
Create `FRONTEND_DESIGN_SPEC.md` later.

---

# DEC-002 — Source-specific ZHMS adapters

Decision:
Treat ZHMS as a collection of source/product layers, not a single API.

Why:
Forensic analysis found separate AWS, hydrology, SYNOP, daily, sea/snow, official forecast, and numerical/static forecast sources.

Consequence:
Each source gets its own adapter and validation path.

---

# DEC-003 — SYNOP is not the universal source

Decision:
Never model the whole portal as a SYNOP feed.

Why:
Current domestic measurements and graphs are primarily represented by AWS/internal monitoring and other products. SYNOP is a separate international/regional layer.

Consequence:
SYNOP can only be used for a specific purpose when its role is evidenced.

---

# DEC-004 — No production TLS bypass

Decision:
TLS verification remains enabled.

Why:
One sandbox showed a local CA trust issue; that did not prove the public site certificate was invalid. Disabling TLS would hide the real problem and weaken security.

Consequence:
Fix CA trust/configuration rather than using `verify=false` or `-k`.

---

# DEC-005 — HTTP 200 is not data validity

Decision:
Validate payload content, not just HTTP status.

Why:
Research showed some bad/unsupported requests returning 200 with `no data`, empty structures, or generic pages.

Consequence:
The adapter must recognize expected source content and schema before accepting it.

---

# DEC-006 — Previous-known-good state

Decision:
Invalid new source data must not overwrite the last valid state.

Why:
Public endpoints can fail, return malformed content, or change schema.

Consequence:
Each important source needs valid-state retention and degradation status.

---

# DEC-007 — Current min/max is derived from fresh observations

Decision:
Calculate current extremes from already collected normalized observations.

Why:
The feature is a current comparison, not a daily aggregate, and the original product requirement explicitly includes temperature, wind, and precipitation extremes.

Eligibility:
measurement timestamp must be within 2h of the common reference timestamp.

Consequence:
No extra upstream scrape is triggered solely for extremes.

---

# DEC-008 — Daily Tn/Tx is not current extremes

Decision:
Do not use daily `Tn`/`Tx` as the implementation of `Aktuelni min/max`.

Why:
Daily aggregates are a different source/product and represent daily minima/maxima.

Consequence:
Current extremes are computed from current eligible station observations.

---

# DEC-009 — No single universal refresh interval

Decision:
Use source-specific and observation-aware scheduling.

Why:
Observed AWS, hydrology, sea/snow, forecast, and SYNOP behaviors differ. Multiple AWS observations did not show a single universal cadence.

Consequence:
The scheduler must remain flexible and should evolve as additional measurements of source behavior are collected.

---

# DEC-010 — Cloud-first development

Decision:
Prefer browser/cloud development because the owner’s main Windows laptop is weak.

Why:
The machine has only about 4 GB RAM and limited free disk, making heavy local stacks undesirable.

Consequence:
GitHub/Codespaces/cloud tools are preferred when they remain free and adequate.

---

# DEC-011 — Free-first infrastructure

Decision:
The initial architecture must favor strictly free services.

Why:
Cost is a hard project constraint.

Consequence:
No paid service becomes a core dependency without explicit owner approval and a demonstrated need.

---

# DEC-012 — Cloudflare-oriented initial backend

Decision:
Use Cloudflare Workers + Cron + D1 as the initial production backend direction, with R2 optional.

Why:
It keeps the architecture relatively simple, serverless, and compatible with the cloud-first constraint.

Consequence:
Supabase is not required in V1.

---

# DEC-013 — Frontend does not scrape ZHMS

Decision:
Frontend communicates with the application API, not directly with ZHMS source pages.

Why:
Direct frontend scraping would duplicate parsing logic, expose source dependence, make freshness harder to control, and reduce reliability.

Consequence:
All ZHMS integration lives in backend adapters.

---

# DEC-014 — Normalize before business logic

Decision:
Keep ZHMS-specific arrays/variables inside adapters and normalize them before business logic.

Why:
The application should not be coupled to source-specific array positions everywhere.

Consequence:
Business functions such as current extremes operate on normalized observations.

---

# DEC-015 — Unknown semantics remain unresolved

Decision:
Do not invent semantics for partially understood fields.

Why:
The forensic work found unresolved fields in SYNOP, daily data, and some source metadata.

Consequence:
Use `UNRESOLVED` / `HYPOTHESIS` status until stronger evidence is obtained.

---

# DEC-016 — User-Agent / pacing is implementation detail

Decision:
Use a meaningful consistent User-Agent and controlled request pacing, not random UA rotation as a core mechanism.

Why:
The project needs responsible source access and low request volume, not deceptive traffic simulation.

Consequence:
Request policy belongs to the source HTTP client/adapter layer.

---

# DEC-017 — Repository is shared AI memory

Decision:
The repository documentation is the durable memory across AI providers and chats.

Why:
The owner may switch AI models/providers during development.

Consequence:
No AI should depend on hidden previous-chat context. Durable project facts must be written to repo documents.

---

# DEC-018 — AI role split

Decision:
Use three AI roles plus owner:

`AI Architect/Mentor -> Coding Agent -> AI Reviewer -> Owner`

Why:
Separating planning, implementation, and review reduces scope drift and makes it easier to use different AI models for different jobs.

Consequence:
Coding agents should receive narrow tasks, not the entire project as one instruction.

---

# DEC-019 — Owner is beginner; AI carries technical burden

Decision:
All AI instructions and explanations must account for the owner’s beginner level.

Why:
The project is intended to let the owner direct the product without requiring them to become a professional developer first.

Consequence:
Break work into small steps and explain technical outcomes clearly.

---

# DEC-020 — No giant rewrite for small tasks

Decision:
Coding agents must make minimal scoped changes.

Why:
Large refactors increase regression risk and make review harder.

Consequence:
Any broad refactor requires explicit architectural justification and documentation.

---

# DEC-021 — Python is research/utility, not the production ingestion architecture

Decision:
Python may be used for research, forensic scripts, data analysis, or utilities, but the production backend direction is TypeScript/Cloudflare Workers.

Why:
The target deployment architecture is serverless/cloud-first and should keep runtime concerns consistent.

Consequence:
The old Python scraper is not the final implementation blueprint.

---

# DEC-022 — Forecast static resources may use conditional caching

Decision:
Use Last-Modified/ETag behavior where confirmed and useful for static forecast resources.

Why:
Research found cache metadata on static forecast HTML/SVG resources.

Consequence:
Re-test exact conditional request semantics during implementation. Do not assume all dynamic endpoints behave the same way.

---

# DEC-023 — HEAD is not a required source capability

Decision:
Do not make HEAD part of the required fetch strategy.

Why:
HEAD frequently returned 403 in research while GET worked.

Consequence:
Use GET and, where useful, conditional GET semantics.

---

# DEC-024 — Owner should not act as a courier between AIs

Decision:
Documentation, not owner memory, transfers context.

Why:
The project may be continued by another model/provider.

Consequence:
The owner supplies artifacts and task status, while AI agents read the repo and continue from durable state.

# ZHMS FORENSIC EVIDENCE
## Public `meteo.co.me` source inventory and observed behavior

Status: RESEARCH EVIDENCE
Purpose: preserve what was actually observed during source investigation so future AIs do not have to rediscover it or turn hypotheses into facts.

Important rule: evidence is not the same as architecture. The architecture document decides how to use the evidence.

---

# 1. GLOBAL FINDINGS

The public ZHMS portal is primarily a classic Apache/PHP/server-rendered site with inline JavaScript and multiple data/product endpoints.

No single modern public JSON/REST API was found that provides all major meteorological data used by the portal.

The public portal is better understood as a collection of separate source/product layers.

Core layers identified:
- AWS current data
- AWS graph/time-series data
- hydrology
- SYNOP
- daily aggregate data
- sea/snow products
- official forecast
- numerical/static forecast products
- static visual products

The most important architectural consequence is:

`SYNOP is NOT the universal feed.`

---

# 2. SOURCE INVENTORY

| ID | Path | Main role | Known output/variables |
|---|---|---|---|
| S01 | `/Meteorologija/aws_m.php` | Current AWS | `var posljednje`, `var stanice` |
| S03 | `/Meteorologija/aws-graph.php?v={tip}&s={ID}` | AWS time series | `var DataAll` |
| S04 | `/Hidrologija/aws_h.php` | Hydrology current + metadata | `var staniceH`, hydrology `var posljednje` |
| S05 | `/Hidrologija/aws-graph-h.php` | Hydrology time series | observed `Data_m` in prior inspection |
| S06 | `/Meteorologija/depese_dnevne.php` | Daily aggregates | `var DataDepeseDnevne` |
| S07 | `/synopT.php` | Montenegro SYNOP | `var sinop` |
| S08 | `/synopT2.php` | regional/Europe SYNOP | `var sinopEU` |
| S09 | `/Meteorologija/TTRR/sneg-talasi.php` | Snow + sea | `snowH2`, `snowT2`, `seaH`, `seaT` |
| S10 | `/page.php?id=31` | Official forecast page | server-rendered forecast content |
| S11 | `/` | Homepage products | inline JS, forecast/alert/sea visuals |
| S12 | homepage sea area | sea display | redundant public display of sea values |
| — | `/Meteorologija/Pr/Gradovi/5danaE/{CITY}-E1.html` ... | Numerical/static forecast | HTML tables, model metadata |

---

# 3. S01/S02 — AWS CURRENT SOURCE

Endpoint:

`/Meteorologija/aws_m.php`

Observed public variables:
- `var posljednje`
- `var stanice`

`var stanice` is station metadata.

A typical station row is approximately:

```text
[stationId, WMO, lat, lon, elevation, name, type, statusFlag]
```

Observed example:
- station ID: `02PDGR10`
- WMO: `13463`
- Podgorica
- latitude approx. `42.43648`
- longitude approx. `19.27199`
- elevation approx. `49`

The station count observed in different research snapshots was not identical, so station count must be treated as dynamic.

The field at index 7 behaves as a status/display flag. Source code inspected during research showed active rows receiving normal marker/dropdown behavior and non-active rows receiving a `notActive` state and “NIJE U FUNKCIJI” type display behavior.

Do not overstate this field as proven physical sensor health.

---

# 4. AWS CURRENT `posljednje`

Observed grouping examples:
- `glavna`
- `klimatoloska`
- `padavinska`

Typical row:

```text
[stationId, type, name, timestamp, T, RR, windSpeed, windDirectionCode, gust]
```

Known semantics:
- `T` = temperature, °C
- `RR` = precipitation, mm
- wind speed = m/s
- gust = m/s
- wind direction = integer code 0–32
- timestamp appears as local-format string such as `31.08.2026 19:40`

Empty string values occur and must not automatically become numeric zero.

Pressure is NOT present in the current row structure observed here.

---

# 5. AWS WIND DIRECTION

AWS wind direction uses a code 0–32.

The portal maps the code using approximately:

`degrees = code * 11.25`

The site also uses compass labels for display.

Do not confuse this with SYNOP `Wdir`, which is expressed differently.

---

# 6. AWS GRAPH — S03

Path:

`/Meteorologija/aws-graph.php?v={tip}&s={ID}`

Expected main variable:

`var DataAll`

Time-series values are represented as timestamp/value pairs.

Known group mappings:

## G1
- `RR`
- `T`
- `H`

Known meaning:
- precipitation;
- temperature;
- humidity.

## G2
- `BRV`
- `PRV`
- `MUV`

Known meaning:
- `BRV` — average/mean wind speed;
- `PRV` — wind direction;
- `MUV` — maximum gust.

`PRV` was confirmed as wind direction through the graph label “Smjer vjetra” and compass mapping.

## G3
- `GR`
- `P`

Known meaning:
- `GR` — portal labels this as `Insolacija (W/m2)`;
- `P` — pressure.

Do not generalize `GR` beyond what the source label proves.

Pressure therefore comes from the time-series graph structure rather than the current `posljednje` row observed in AWS current source.

---

# 7. HYDROLOGY — S04

Endpoint:

`/Hidrologija/aws_h.php`

This endpoint exists publicly.

An earlier contradictory conclusion was caused by testing an incorrect path and must be considered superseded.

Observed variables:
- `var staniceH`
- hydrology `var posljednje`

`staniceH` is grouped by watershed, observed groups including:
- `jadranski`
- `crnomorski`

A typical station metadata row is approximately:

```text
[id, WMO-or-placeholder, lat, lon, elevation, name, stationType, river, flag]
```

Current hydrology values observed in `posljednje` include:
- type;
- name;
- timestamp;
- water level;
- water temperature.

One inspected snapshot contained mostly hourly timestamps, but a universal hydrology cadence was NOT proved.

---

# 8. HYDROLOGY GRAPH — S05

Endpoint:

`/Hidrologija/aws-graph-h.php`

Used for hydrology time series.

Prior inspection observed a `Data_m` style time-series variable.

Exact long-term schema should still be validated by the implementation adapter before being considered locked.

---

# 9. DAILY DATA — S06

Endpoint:

`/Meteorologija/depese_dnevne.php`

Variable:

`var DataDepeseDnevne`

Observed fields:
- `naziv`
- `sifra`
- `datum`
- `RR`
- `Tn`
- `Tx`
- `USN`

Observed data covered multiple recent dates.

`Tn` and `Tx` are daily aggregate temperature values.

They are NOT current min/max values for the application’s `Aktuelni min/max` function.

`USN` meaning was not sufficiently proven and must remain unresolved until stronger evidence is obtained.

---

# 10. SEA / SNOW — S09

Endpoint:

`/Meteorologija/TTRR/sneg-talasi.php`

Observed variables:
- `snowH2`
- `snowT2`
- `seaH`
- `seaT`

Observed facts:
- snow content includes a time around 8h;
- snow table explicitly labels `Visina snijega u 8h (cm)`;
- sea data can have a separate time, and an observed case used approximately 14h;
- therefore sea must NOT be assumed to be available only at 8h;
- homepage sea display can duplicate equivalent sea values from another presentation layer.

Dedicated source should normally be preferred when it provides the same underlying data more directly.

---

# 11. SYNOP — S07/S08

Montenegro source:

`/synopT.php`

Variable:

`sinop`

Regional source:

`/synopT2.php`

Variable:

`sinopEU`

Observed SYNOP fields/examples include:
- `sifra`
- `naziv`
- `sat`
- `T`
- `TTR`
- `P`
- `P0`
- `Ws`
- `Wdir`
- `RH`
- `OBL`
- `ww`
- other source-specific fields.

Some individual SYNOP fields were not fully decoded.

Examples of unresolved or partially resolved fields from research:
- `indRR`
- `indPO`
- `VBNobl`
- `ww`
- `Wpast`
- `G2.talasi`
- `G2.SPM`

These must not be assigned invented semantics.

Most importantly:

SYNOP is a separate layer. It is not the source from which the whole portal is populated.

---

# 12. OFFICIAL FORECAST — S10

Endpoint:

`/page.php?id=31`

Contains official forecast information, including text and seafarer-related content.

The page is part of the CMS/server-rendered site and should not be mistaken for a modern JSON API.

---

# 13. NUMERICAL FORECAST / STATIC FORECAST PRODUCTS

Observed paths follow forms such as:

`/Meteorologija/Pr/Gradovi/5danaE/{CITY}-E1.html`

through later days such as E2, E3, E4, E5.

Observed table concepts:
- day/date;
- Tmin;
- Tmax;
- 00, 03, 06, 09, 12, 15, 18, 21 UTC;
- precipitation;
- humidity;
- weather symbol;
- wind symbol;
- model;
- coordinates;
- elevation;
- model height.

Static forecast resources were observed with HTTP cache metadata such as `Last-Modified` and `ETag`.

One research report indicated `If-Modified-Since` could produce 304 behavior while `If-None-Match` behavior appeared less consistent. This is implementation evidence to re-test, not a universal promise for every file.

---

# 14. STATIC VISUAL PRODUCTS

Observed examples include:
- `cgprognoza-A.svg`
- `cgprognoza-B.svg`
- `jjadran.svg`

These can be large SVG products and are not necessarily convenient as a stable machine-readable source.

Some weather/wind symbol semantics are represented through static SVG/filename structures.

Where a source is visual-only, the backend should not invent a parallel data schema without evidence.

---

# 15. HOMEPAGE / CMS BEHAVIOR

Homepage and CMS pages were observed with cache-control directives such as:
- `no-store`
- `no-cache`
- `must-revalidate`
- `Pragma: no-cache`
- old `Expires` value

A PHP session cookie was observed on CMS pages.

Session dependence for the key AWS/hydrology data endpoints was not proven.

---

# 16. HTTP METHOD OBSERVATIONS

GET requests to key endpoints generally returned 200 during low-volume testing.

HEAD requests frequently returned 403.

Therefore HEAD must not be required for source validation.

Use GET-based validation and, where supported, conditional GET behavior for static/cacheable resources.

---

# 17. HTTP 200 VS DATA VALIDITY

A number of invalid/unsupported requests returned HTTP 200 with content such as:
- `no data`;
- empty `DataAll`;
- generic shells/pages.

Therefore:

`HTTP status == transport result, not semantic validity.`

Adapter parsers must validate the expected variable/structure.

---

# 18. TRUE 404

Nonexistent paths can return actual 404 responses.

This does not remove the requirement for application-level validation because many malformed or unsupported requests still return 200.

---

# 19. TLS EVIDENCE

The public site certificate was valid for `www.meteo.co.me` and browsers could access the site.

One curl/sandbox environment reported a local issuer trust error (`ssl_verify_result 20`).

This was treated as a local trust-chain/runtime issue, not proof that the public server certificate was invalid.

Production must keep TLS verification enabled.

---

# 20. ROBOTS / SITEMAP

During research:
- `robots.txt` returned 200 with no effective `Disallow` rules observed;
- sitemap request returned 404.

These observations are technical, not a legal authorization.

Do not infer legal permission solely from robots.txt behavior.

---

# 21. REFRESH / LONGITUDINAL OBSERVATIONS

Multiple AWS snapshots over a longer observation window showed some stations moving in approximately 10-minute patterns, while other stations showed slower/hourly timestamps.

Another shorter observation window showed no changes.

Conclusion:

The refresh/publication cadence is NOT uniform enough to justify a single hard-coded global interval.

One observed transition suggested that public content for some AWS observations could appear around 10 minutes after an earlier measurement transition in that particular window, but publication delay was not directly measurable in a general way.

Hydrology showed many hourly timestamps in one snapshot, with other times present.

Sea/snow had their own reporting terms.

Forecast resources had a separate generation/update lifecycle.

SYNOP has its own reporting conventions and must not be used to infer AWS cadence.

---

# 22. WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED

At the time of this evidence package, keep these unresolved unless further tests prove them:
- exact universal AWS publication latency;
- exact universal station update cadence;
- exact hydrology cadence across all stations;
- all meanings of unknown SYNOP fields;
- definitive meaning of `USN` in daily data;
- full timezone semantics for every endpoint/source;
- complete semantics of all status flags;
- every detail of static SVG weather/wind symbol meaning.

Do not silently turn hypotheses into contracts.

---

# 23. IMPLEMENTATION SAFETY RULE

For every source adapter, preserve the following chain:

`fetch -> recognize -> parse -> validate -> normalize -> persist`

Failure at any stage must be observable.

If parsing/validation fails:
- do not publish new invalid data;
- keep previous-known-good when possible;
- mark source degraded;
- capture enough evidence for debugging.

---

# 24. EVIDENCE CONFIDENCE LANGUAGE

Use:

`CONFIRMED` — directly observed/verified in source behavior.

`SUPPORTED` — strongly supported by multiple observations, but not complete proof of every edge case.

`HYPOTHESIS` — plausible interpretation needing more validation.

`UNRESOLVED` — no safe semantic assignment yet.

This language should be used in future forensic updates.

Drafting a beginner-friendly owner explanation and a minimal coding-agent task with repo layout and acceptance checks.

Kao tvoj **AI Architect / Mentor** pročitao sam svih 6 dokumenata zajedničke memorije:

* `MASTER_SPECIFICATION.md` — šta app mora da radi (backend-first)
* `ARCHITECTURE.md:2` — Cloudflare Workers + Cron + D1 + React
* `TASKS.md:14` — TASK-001 je sljedeći
* `DECISIONS.md:14` — DEC-010 cloud-first, DEC-012 Workers, DEC-017 repo je memorija
* `ZHMS_FORENSIC_EVIDENCE.md` + `REVIEW.md`

### Gdje smo sada?

* `C:\Users\Administratör\Documents\Default Project` je prazan — nema `git`, nema koda.
* 6 dokumenata postoji samo u `Downloads\montenegro-weather-project` — nisu još u repo-u.
* To je normalno za start. Repo je prazan = nema memorije za AI agente.

### Veliki cilj razložen na 1 mali korak

Veliki cilj: Montenegro Weather App koja čita ZHMS `meteo.co.me` preko backend adaptera.

Ne radimo sve odjednom. Pravilo `MASTER_SPECIFICATION.md:25` = 1 atomski task.

**SLEDEĆI TASK = TASK-001 — Repository skeleton**

Za apsolutnog početnika, ovo znači:

1.  Napravimo fascikle kao ormar za projekat (`src/`, `tests/`, `docs/`)
2.  Kopiramo 6 dokumenata u repo da svaki AI može da ih čita
3.  Dodamo `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `wrangler.toml` — bez njih laptop ne zna da je ovo Cloudflare projekat
4.  Dodamo najmanji Worker koji vraća `Hello` i 1 prazan test
5.  Provjerimo: `npm install` radi, `npm test` prolazi, `npm run build` prolazi

Zašto baš ovo prvo? Bez skeleta `ARCHITECTURE.md:4` i `TASKS.md` nemaju gdje da žive, a i tvoj slab laptop (4GB RAM) mora da radi cloud-first — zato odmah podešavamo `GitHub + Cloudflare` a ne težak lokalni setup.

### Zadatak za Coding Agenta (kopiraj/pejstuj mu)

> **TASK-001 — Repository skeleton — JEDINI zadatak**
> Radi u `C:\Users\Administratör\Documents\Default Project`
> 1. `git init` + `.gitignore` (node_modules, .wrangler, dist)
> 2. Kopiraj 6 md fajlova iz Downloads u root
> 3. Kreiraj `package.json` (name: montenegro-weather, type: module, scripts: dev/build/test/typecheck)
> 4. `src/index.ts` — minimal Cloudflare Worker `fetch` handler koji vraća JSON `{status:"ok"}`
> 5. `wrangler.toml` + `tsconfig.json` + `vitest.config.ts`
> 6. `tests/hello.test.ts` — 1 test koji prolazi
> 7. `README.md` sa uputstvom za cloud dev
> NE DIRAJ ništa iz PHASE 1-14. Samo skeleton. Minimalne izmjene.
> Acceptance: `npm install && npm test && npm run build` prolaze.

### Šta će Reviewer provjeriti (upis u `REVIEW.md`)

* Da li postoje svi fajlovi iz `ARCHITECTURE.md:4`?
* Da li je TLS ostao uključen, nema `verify=false` (`DECISIONS.md:7`)?
* Da li testovi i build prolaze?
* Da li nema viška koda van TASK-001?

### Tvoja provjera kao Owner (30 sekundi)

Nakon što Coding Agent završi, ti samo ukucaš:
`npm test` -> vidiš zeleno `1 passed`
`npm run build` -> nema greške

**Pitanje za tebe:** Da li da odmah pokrenem Coding Agenta za ovaj TASK-001? Ako kažeš DA, nećeš morati ništa ručno da kopiraš — ja ću mu dati instrukciju, a ti ćeš samo potvrditi rezultat.

Takođe ću nakon toga u `TASKS.md:14` staviti `TASK-001: IN PROGRESS -> REVIEW`.

parts.text: Creating a beginner-friendly first task with simple analogies and step-by-step verification for a Codespace setup.
Drafting a beginner-friendly Codespace task with copy-paste steps and a simple verification command.

Razumijem, hvala ti. Pričaću ti najprostijim jezikom, bez stručnih riječi.

**Gdje si sada:**
Tvoj repo `MeteoMNEv6` na GitHubu je prazan. Ima samo `README.md`. Radiš u Codespace-u — to je odlično, baš tako treba (DEC-010) jer ne opterećuje tvoj laptop.

**Velika slika u 1 rečenici:**
Pravimo aplikaciju za vrijeme u Crnoj Gori. Prvo pravimo "kuhinju" iza (da pokupi podatke sa ZHMS-a), pa tek onda ono što korisnik vidi na ekranu. Zato se zove backend-first.

**Ne brini — ne moraš sve odjednom. Samo 1 mali korak:**

### Korak 1 od 20: Temelj kuće (TASK-001)

Zamislimo da gradiš kuću. Ovaj korak je samo da napravimo prazne sobe i da provjerimo da struja radi. Ništa o vremenu još ne programiramo.

**Šta će Coding Agent (ti u Codespace-u) da uradi — prekopiraj ovo:**

To je JEDAN zadatak. Kad ga završiš, imaćeš:

1. Fascikle `src/` i `tests/` — kao prazne sobe
2. 6 papira sa uputstvima (`MASTER_SPECIFICATION.md` itd.) kopirana u repo — to je naša zajednička memorija da svaki AI zna gdje smo stali
3. 3 mala fajla: `package.json`, `wrangler.toml`, `src/index.ts` koji samo kažu "Hello, radi!" — da provjerimo da Codespace radi
4. Jedan mali test da vidimo zeleno svijetlo

**Kako ćeš znati da je uspjelo?**
U Codespace terminalu ukucaš:
`npm test`
Treba da piše `1 passed` — znači temelj je dobar. To je sve.

**Šta NE treba da razumiješ sada:**
Riječi kao `adapter`, `D1`, `Cron` — to su samo alati za kasnije. Preskoči ih. Ja ću ti svaki put objasniti novu riječ kad dođe red na nju.

Hoćeš li da ti ja sada napišem tačno šta da nalijepiš u Codespace da se ovaj prvi temelj napravi automatski?

Reci samo `da` i ja ti dajem spremne komande — ne moraš ništa da smišljaš sam.

1: # MASTER SPECIFICATION
2: # Montenegro Weather App
3: ## Project Source of Truth + AI Development Operating Manual
4: 
5: Status: ACTIVE
6: Version: 1.0
7: Scope: Product requirements, owner context, development workflow, global constraints, backend-first direction.
8: 
9: ---
10: 
11: ## 0. PURPOSE
12: 
13: This document is the primary onboarding document for any new AI assistant, architect, coding agent, reviewer, or developer entering the project without access to the previous chat history.
14: 
15: It must explain not only what the application should become, but also how the project must be developed with the owner.
16: 
17: The project must never depend on one AI conversation as its memory. The repository is the shared memory.
18: 
19: This document must be read before implementation.
20: 
21: Supporting documents:
22: - `ZHMS_FORENSIC_EVIDENCE.md` — detailed evidence about public ZHMS sources and HTTP/data behavior.
23: - `ARCHITECTURE.md` — current technical architecture and implementation boundaries.
24: - `TASKS.md` — atomic development tasks and status.
25: - `DECISIONS.md` — durable decisions and reasons.
26: - `REVIEW.md` — technical review results, when available.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: # 1. OWNER / USER CONTEXT
31: 
32: The project owner is the product owner and final decision-maker. The owner has strong intuition about the product and its desired functionality, but is an absolute beginner in practical software development.
33: 
34: Therefore, every AI helping on the project must act as BOTH:
35: 
36: 1. technical executor / technical problem solver;
37: 2. technical mentor for a beginner.
38: 
39: The owner should not have to remember project history or manually transfer large amounts of context between AIs.
40: 
41: The owner should not be treated like a professional backend/frontend engineer.
42: 
43: The AI must explain technical work in clear language and in small steps, while doing the technically difficult work itself whenever possible.
44: 
45: Preferred interaction pattern:
46: 
47: `Goal -> Small Task -> Explain -> Implement -> Test -> Verify -> Next Task`
48: 
49: Avoid dumping twenty unrelated steps on the owner at once.
50: 
51: The owner should understand:
52: - what is being built;
53: - why it is being built;
54: - what changed;
55: - how to verify it;
56: - what decision, if any, needs owner approval.
57: 
58: The owner should NOT be a messenger between AIs.
59: 
60: ---
61: 
62: # 2. OWNER DEVELOPMENT CONDITIONS
63: 
64: Primary development machine:
65: - Windows 10 laptop
66: - Intel i3 class CPU
67: - 4 GB RAM
68: - approximately 5 GB free disk space
69: 
70: This machine is weak for heavy local development.
71: 
72: Therefore the preferred development strategy is cloud-first / browser-first.
73: 
74: Possible development tools:
75: - GitHub
76: - GitHub Codespaces or another free cloud development environment when its free allowance is sufficient
77: - browser-based terminals/editors where practical
78: - GitHub Actions
79: 
80: Secondary device:
81: - Android Samsung Galaxy A54
82: - Termux available/possible
83: - Python available/possible
84: - Node.js available/possible
85: 
86: The phone is a supporting device, not the main production development environment.
87: 
88: ---
89: 
90: # 3. COST CONSTRAINT
91: 
92: At the beginning of the project, recommend only adequate services that can be used strictly for free.
93: 
94: Do not build the architecture around paid services when a free and adequate option exists.
95: 
96: For every external service, the AI should consider:
97: - actual free availability;
98: - relevant free limits;
99: - whether the project can remain functional within those limits;
100: - vendor lock-in risk;
101: - whether the service is actually necessary.
102: 
103: Do not introduce a service merely because it is popular.
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: # 4. PRODUCT GOAL
108: 
109: Build a modern Montenegro weather application that provides useful public meteorological information published by the Hydrometeorological Service of Montenegro (ZHMS) through the public `meteo.co.me` portal.
110: 
111: The application should be:
112: - mobile-first;
113: - responsive on desktop and mobile web;
114: - PWA-ready;
115: - later packageable for Android and iOS, preferably with Capacitor after the web/backend foundation is stable.
116: 
117: The app should not simply copy the ZHMS website. It should expose useful information in a cleaner application-oriented data model.
118: 
119: ---
120: 
121: # 5. CORE PRODUCT NAVIGATION
122: 
123: Main areas:
124: 
125: 1. `Odabrana stanica`
126: 2. `Sve stanice`
127: 3. `Prognoza`
128: 
129: The final visual design will be specified later in a separate frontend specification.
130: 
131: The current master defines the functional data requirements, not final pixel-level UI.
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: # 6. SELECTED STATION FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
136: 
137: The application must be able to show for the selected station:
138: - current temperature prominently;
139: - weather icon / weather state;
140: - humidity;
141: - wind;
142: - pressure;
143: - precipitation;
144: - gust;
145: - insolation;
146: - measurement time / freshness context;
147: - time-series charts.
148: 
149: Target chart groups:
150: 1. temperature + humidity;
151: 2. precipitation;
152: 3. wind;
153: 4. pressure;
154: 5. insolation.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: # 7. ALL STATIONS FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
159: 
160: The app must support:
161: - station list;
162: - current observation data;
163: - search/filtering;
164: - station detail;
165: - map location;
166: - current temperature on the map;
167: - station status/freshness information;
168: - selecting a station as the selected station;
169: - sea temperature data;
170: - snow data.
171: 
172: A station detail must expose the same essential observation/time-series information needed by the selected-station view.
173: 
174: ---
175: 
176: # 8. CURRENT MIN/MAX FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
177: 
178: The `Aktuelni min/max` feature is a derived feature, not a copy of ZHMS daily Tn/Tx.
179: 
180: It must include:
181: 
182: Temperature:
183: - current hottest eligible station;
184: - current coldest eligible station.
185: 
186: Wind:
187: - current strongest eligible wind;
188: - current weakest eligible wind.
189: 
190: Precipitation:
191: - current highest eligible precipitation;
192: - current lowest eligible precipitation.
193: 
194: Eligibility rule:
195: - determine one common current reference timestamp from the newest relevant station measurement time;
196: - include a station only if its observation timestamp is within 2 hours of that reference;
197: - exactly 2 hours is included;
198: - invalid/missing observations are excluded;
199: - ineligible/inactive source records are excluded;
200: - ties must be supported;
201: - no eligible candidates must produce an explicit unavailable/no-candidates state.
202: 
203: Do NOT issue extra ZHMS requests only to calculate extremes. Reuse already fetched and validated current observations.
204: 
205: Do NOT confuse this with daily Tmin/Tx from the daily aggregate source.
206: 
207: ---
208: 
209: # 9. FORECAST REQUIREMENTS
210: 
211: ## 9.1 Official forecast
212: 
213: Support:
214: - official text forecast;
215: - multiple forecast days;
216: - seafarer information where published;
217: - related public visual products where appropriate.
218: 
219: ## 9.2 Numerical forecast
220: 
221: Support:
222: - model selection where source provides it;
223: - location/station selection;
224: - multiple forecast days;
225: - hourly data;
226: - temperature;
227: - humidity;
228: - precipitation;
229: - weather symbol;
230: - wind information;
231: - model metadata;
232: - source timestamps/metadata where available.
233: 
234: ---
235: 
236: # 10. CRITICAL SOURCE PRINCIPLE
237: 
238: The ZHMS portal is NOT one universal weather API.
239: 
240: It is a set of different public data/product sources.
241: 
242: The backend must therefore use source-specific adapters.
243: 
244: Examples include:
245: - AWS current observations;
246: - AWS time series;
247: - hydrology;
248: - SYNOP;
249: - daily data;
250: - sea/snow;
251: - official forecast;
252: - numerical forecast/static forecast products.
253: 
254: ---
255: 
256: # 11. CRITICAL SYNOP RULE
257: 
258: The entire portal must NEVER be modeled as “one big SYNOP feed”.
259: 
260: Public views of current domestic measurements, graphs, and many operational tables are primarily backed by AWS/internal monitoring and other products.
261: 
262: SYNOP is a separate international/regional layer.
263: 
264: Therefore:
265: - SYNOP gets its own source adapter;
266: - SYNOP may be primary, secondary, or cross-check for a particular parameter only when evidence supports that role;
267: - SYNOP must never automatically replace AWS for all data.
268: 
269: ---
270: 
271: # 12. DATA FRESHNESS GOAL
272: 
273: The target is that the app should normally lag the newest publicly available ZHMS data by roughly no more than several minutes, with an aspirational target around 3 minutes.
274: 
275: This is a public-source freshness goal, not a claim that every source changes every 3 minutes.
276: 
277: The scheduler must be source-specific and observation-aware.
278: 
279: Do not hard-code one universal refresh interval for every source.
280: 
281: ---
282: 
283: # 13. TIME SEMANTICS
284: 
285: Always distinguish:
286: - measurement time;
287: - publication time, if observable;
288: - backend fetch time;
289: - storage time.
290: 
291: Fetch time must never silently replace source measurement time.
292: 
293: Freshness calculations should be based on source observation/measurement timestamps where available.
294: 
295: ---
296: 
297: # 14. BACKEND-FIRST DEVELOPMENT
298: 
299: The immediate development focus is the backend/data layer.
300: 
301: The final frontend visual specification will be produced later.
302: 
303: Do not spend early project effort on pixel-perfect frontend design before:
304: - source ingestion;
305: - normalization;
306: - persistence;
307: - freshness;
308: - validation;
309: - API contracts;
310: - monitoring;
311: - tests
312: are stable enough.
313: 
314: ---
315: 
316: # 15. TARGET PRODUCTION ARCHITECTURE
317: 
318: Preferred initial architecture:
319: 
320: - Cloudflare Workers — backend/API and ingestion execution
321: - Cloudflare Cron — scheduled ingestion
322: - Cloudflare D1 — structured application data
323: - optional Cloudflare R2 — raw snapshots/debugging when justified
324: - React + Vite — frontend
325: - GitHub — source control/shared memory
326: - GitHub Actions — CI/test automation
327: - PWA-first — initial delivery
328: - Capacitor later — Android/iOS packaging
329: 
330: No Supabase is required for V1 unless later evidence shows a real need.
331: 
332: ---
333: 
334: # 16. RAW VS NORMALIZED DATA
335: 
336: Keep a strict separation:
337: 
338: `Raw ZHMS source -> Parse -> Validate -> Normalize -> Persist -> Derive -> API`
339: 
340: The frontend must consume normalized application models, not raw ZHMS structures.
341: 
342: Raw snapshots may be retained when useful for:
343: - debugging;
344: - schema change detection;
345: - forensic reproduction;
346: - audit/troubleshooting.
347: 
348: ---
349: 
350: # 17. VALIDATION RULES
351: 
352: HTTP status is not sufficient.
353: 
354: `200 OK` does not guarantee valid data.
355: 
356: Examples of failure responses seen during forensic work included:
357: - `no data`;
358: - empty `DataAll`;
359: - generic page/shell content.
360: 
361: Every adapter must validate expected content and schema.
362: 
363: Missing data is NOT zero.
364: 
365: Stale data is NOT live data.
366: 
367: Invalid new data must NOT overwrite previous known-good data.
368: 
369: ---
370: 
371: # 18. PREVIOUS-KNOWN-GOOD
372: 
373: For important sources, keep the latest valid state.
374: 
375: On invalid/failing refresh:
376: - reject invalid payload;
377: - keep previous valid state;
378: - mark source degraded/stale/error as appropriate;
379: - record the failure;
380: - preserve `last_successful_sync` information.
381: 
382: ---
383: 
384: # 19. TLS
385: 
386: Production HTTPS verification must remain enabled.
387: 
388: Do not use `verify=false`, `-k`, or an equivalent permanent TLS bypass.
389: 
390: One research environment showed a local CA trust problem while the public site certificate was valid for `www.meteo.co.me`.
391: 
392: If a runtime cannot validate the chain, fix trust configuration or explicitly provide a correct CA bundle when justified.
393: 
394: ---
395: 
396: # 20. HTTP REQUEST BEHAVIOR
397: 
398: Known research observations:
399: - GET generally works on key endpoints;
400: - HEAD often returns 403 and therefore must not be a core dependency;
401: - key dynamic data endpoints generally lacked Last-Modified/ETag in testing;
402: - some static forecast resources do provide cache metadata;
403: - low-volume testing did not establish a global rate limit.
404: 
405: Do not perform aggressive probing in production.
406: 
407: ---
408: 
409: # 21. USER-AGENT / REQUEST PACING
410: 
411: This is implementation detail, not product functionality.
412: 
413: Preferred behavior:
414: - use a consistent, meaningful User-Agent where appropriate;
415: - keep request pacing controlled;
416: - prefer bulk/minimal source requests;
417: - reuse cached/validated data;
418: - avoid unnecessary repeated calls.
419: 
420: Do not design the system around deceptive random User-Agent rotation or fake “human simulation”.
421: 
422: The goal is responsible, low-load access to the public source.
423: 
424: ---
425: 
426: # 22. AI DEVELOPMENT WORKFLOW — CRITICAL
427: 
428: The project is designed to work with multiple AIs and potentially different models/providers.
429: 
430: The project must remain transferable between AI chats.
431: 
432: Workflow:
433: 
434: `OWNER -> AI ARCHITECT / TECHNICAL MENTOR -> CODING AGENT -> AI REVIEWER -> OWNER`
435: 
436: ## 22.1 AI Architect / Technical Mentor
437: 
438: Responsibilities:
439: - read the project documentation;
440: - understand owner context;
441: - understand source evidence;
442: - break large goals into small tasks;
443: - explain tasks to the owner in beginner-friendly language;
444: - propose technical choices;
445: - guard architecture and scope;
446: - update durable project documentation when decisions change.
447: 
448: ## 22.2 Coding Agent
449: 
450: Reads at minimum:
451: - `MASTER_SPECIFICATION.md`;
452: - `ARCHITECTURE.md`;
453: - `TASKS.md`;
454: - `DECISIONS.md`;
455: - relevant portions of `ZHMS_FORENSIC_EVIDENCE.md`.
456: 
457: Implements ONE concrete task at a time.
458: 
459: It must not reinterpret the entire project from scratch for each task.
460: 
461: ## 22.3 AI Reviewer
462: 
463: Checks:
464: - functional correctness;
465: - tests;
466: - security;
467: - architecture;
468: - regressions;
469: - source behavior assumptions;
470: - stale/fresh logic;
471: - whether the coding agent implemented something not requested.
472: 
473: ## 22.4 Owner
474: 
475: The owner:
476: - prioritizes;
477: - approves important decisions;
478: - accepts/rejects outcomes;
479: - decides when a task is product-complete.
480: 
481: The owner is NOT the project’s human message bus.
482: 
483: ---
484: 
485: # 23. SHARED MEMORY DOCUMENTS
486: 
487: The repository should contain at least:
488: 
489: ```text
490: MASTER_SPECIFICATION.md
491: ZHMS_FORENSIC_EVIDENCE.md
492: ARCHITECTURE.md
493: TASKS.md
494: DECISIONS.md
495: REVIEW.md
496: ```
497: 
498: Optional as complexity grows:
499: 
500: ```text
501: SOURCE_CONTRACTS.md
502: TEST_STRATEGY.md
503: RUNBOOK.md
504: ```
505: 
506: ---
507: 
508: # 24. DOCUMENTATION LAYERS
509: 
510: Three concepts must never be mixed:
511: 
512: ## Requirement
513: What the product must do.
514: 
515: ## Evidence
516: What the source/system has actually been shown to do.
517: 
518: ## Decision
519: How the project has chosen to implement something.
520: 
521: Example:
522: 
523: Requirement: current station observations.
524: 
525: Evidence: `aws_m.php` exposes current AWS data through `var posljednje` and station metadata through `var stanice`.
526: 
527: Decision: create a dedicated AWS adapter and normalize it into the application’s station/observation model.
528: 
529: ---
530: 
531: # 25. TASK DECOMPOSITION PRINCIPLE
532: 
533: Never assign the whole application as one coding task.
534: 
535: Prefer atomic tasks such as:
536: - project skeleton;
537: - AWS fetch adapter;
538: - AWS parser;
539: - AWS validator;
540: - normalized station model;
541: - persistence;
542: - freshness logic;
543: - current station API;
544: - current extremes;
545: - time-series ingestion;
546: - hydrology adapter;
547: - forecast adapter;
548: - monitoring;
549: - tests.
550: 
551: Each task must have clear acceptance criteria.
552: 
553: ---
554: 
555: # 26. DEFINITION OF DONE
556: 
557: A task is done only when:
558: - the requirement is tracked in `TASKS.md`;
559: - the required implementation exists;
560: - tests cover the expected behavior;
561: - relevant edge cases are considered;
562: - architecture remains coherent;
563: - documentation is updated;
564: - decisions are recorded when applicable;
565: - the reviewer has no critical unresolved issue;
566: - the owner can understand what was delivered.
567: 
568: ---
569: 
570: # 27. PROHIBITIONS
571: 
572: The project must NOT:
573: - copy the old Python scraper and treat it as the final architecture;
574: - treat SYNOP as the universal source;
575: - disable TLS verification;
576: - trust HTTP 200 without payload validation;
577: - treat missing values as zeros;
578: - treat stale observations as current;
579: - confuse daily Tn/Tx with current extremes;
580: - make extra ZHMS requests solely to calculate current extremes;
581: - let invalid payloads overwrite previous known-good data;
582: - introduce paid infrastructure as a dependency when a free adequate option exists;
583: - directly scrape ZHMS from the production frontend;
584: - introduce unnecessary microservices;
585: - invent meanings for unresolved fields;
586: - rewrite large parts of the codebase for a small task without justification;
587: - change architectural decisions silently.
588: 
589: ---
590: 
591: # 28. CURRENT BACKEND PRIORITY ORDER
592: 
593: 1. repository/project skeleton
594: 2. environment and CI
595: 3. source adapter infrastructure
596: 4. AWS current source
597: 5. AWS normalization
598: 6. persistence
599: 7. freshness
600: 8. selected/current station API
601: 9. all stations API
602: 10. current min/max
603: 11. AWS time series
604: 12. hydrology
605: 13. sea/snow
606: 14. SYNOP
607: 15. daily data
608: 16. official forecast
609: 17. numerical forecast
610: 18. monitoring/observability
611: 19. automated tests and hardening
612: 20. frontend integration
613: 
614: ---
615: 
616: # 29. FUTURE FRONTEND SPECIFICATION
617: 
618: Create later:
619: 
620: `FRONTEND_DESIGN_SPEC.md`
621: 
622: That document will consume the stable backend/API model plus the original functional ideas and screenshot references.
623: 
624: It should define:
625: - layout;
626: - components;
627: - responsive behavior;
628: - mobile UX;
629: - desktop UX;
630: - charts;
631: - maps;
632: - forecast presentation;
633: - states;
634: - loading/error/stale behavior;
635: - typography and visual hierarchy.
636: 
637: ---
638: 
639: # 30. FINAL OPERATING RULE
640: 
641: A new AI entering the project must behave as if this document is the project’s institutional memory.
642: 
643: It must not require the owner to reconstruct the history of previous chats.
644: 
645: Before implementation, it must read this document and the relevant supporting documents.
646: 
647: When evidence is missing, mark it as unresolved instead of silently inventing an answer.
648: 
649: When a new technical decision is made, record it in `DECISIONS.md`.
650: 
651: When the architecture changes, update `ARCHITECTURE.md`.
652: 
653: When work is planned or completed, update `TASKS.md`.
654: 
655: The owner is the product owner and decision-maker; the AI is responsible for carrying as much of the technical burden as safely and practically possible.

parts.text: Investigating CI typecheck failure by comparing local and CI environments and identifying potential TypeScript type issues.
Pinpointing the missing DOM types for fetch in the CI typecheck configuration.

Provjerio sam GitHub — **poštar je stigao, ali automatski pregled je pao**.

Na GitHub Actions piše:
* `Run npm ci` — ✅ prošao
* `Run npm run typecheck` — ❌ pao
* `Run npm test` — preskočen (jer je typecheck pao)

To znači da TypeScript kaže "ima greška u kucanju" iako su testovi kod tebe prošli. To je ona provjera `npm run typecheck` koja gleda svako slovo.

**Da vidimo tačno šta mu smeta — 1 komanda u Codespace-u:**

Nalijepi ovo:
```bash
npm run typecheck
```

Kopiraj mi **sve crveno** što izađe (cijeli tekst greške) pa ću odmah da ispravim. Ne moraš ništa da razumiješ, samo copy/paste crvenog.

Jesi za?
Diagnosing a Vitest type mismatch where vi restoreAllMocks return type conflicts with HookListener Awaitable void expectation.

Provereno — **sada je zeleno** ✅

`262152a` — `status: completed`, `conclusion: success` — znači automatski pregled kaže sve je tačno, i `typecheck` i `test`.

**Da i papir bude tačan — zadnja sitnica:**
```bash
python3 -c "
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path('TASKS.md')
t = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
t = t.replace('## TASK-011 — HTTP client wrapper\nStatus: TODO', '## TASK-011 — HTTP client wrapper\nStatus: DONE', 1)
p.write_text(t, encoding='utf-8')
print('TASKS popravljen')
"
cat >> REVIEW.md <<'EOF'

---
## REVIEW-003 — TASK-011 postar
Date: 2026-09-02
Reviewer: AI Reviewer

Findings: zhmsFetch GET+UA+timeout OK, typecheck OK, 4 tests PASS, CI success

EOF
git add TASKS.md REVIEW.md
git commit -m "REVIEW-003: TASK-011 PASS"
git push
echo "--- UPISANO ---"
```

Kad vidiš `UPISANO`, poštar je zvanično gotov.

Hoćemo li sada sljedeći kalup — da naučimo poštara da prepozna **da li je pismo pravo vrijeme ili prazno "no data"**? To je sledeći mali korak, opet 1 komanda.

Hvala ti — to je važna promjena i kao profesionalac ću je odmah zapisati svuda da se ne zaboravi.

**Kao profesionalac biram: prvo `min/max` sa novim pravilom `1 sat`, pa tek onda `stranica`.**

Zašto?
* `Diskretno vrijeme` je sitan detalj na stranici, ali da bi stranica mogla da ga pokaže, **API prvo mora da pošalje to vrijeme**. Zato prvo pravimo `min/max` da vraća i `vrijeme mjerenja`, pa onda stranica samo to prikaže sitnim slovima.
* Ako bi pravili stranicu prije `min/max`, morali bi je poslije opet prepravljati.

**Tvoja nova odluka koju ću odmah upisati svuda (da svaki AI zna):**
* **Bilo je:** stanica važi ako je mjerila u zadnja 2 sata
* **Sada je:** stanica važi ako je mjerila u zadnjih **1 sat** (strože, svježije)
* **Novo:** na stranici kod `min/max` piše sitno `mjereno u 20:50` pored temperature

cat > src/lib/timeseriesDb.ts <<'EOF'
export async function saveTimeseries(db: D1Database, stationId: string, param: string, points: {ts:number,value:number|null}[]): Promise<void> {
  for(const p of points){
    if(p.value==null) continue;
    await db.prepare(`INSERT INTO station_timeseries (station_id, ts, param, value) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?) ON CONFLICT(station_id, ts, param) DO UPDATE SET value=excluded.value`).bind(stationId, p.ts, param, p.value).run();
  }
}
export async function loadTimeseries(db: D1Database, stationId: string, param: string, limit: number = 48): Promise<{ts:number,value:number}[]> {
  const {results} = await db.prepare(`SELECT ts, value FROM station_timeseries WHERE station_id=? AND param=? ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT ?`).bind(stationId, param, limit).all();
  return (results as any[]).map(r=> ({ts:r.ts, value:r.value})).reverse();
}
EOF

Javi šta vidiš na grafiku — da li rade dugmići i tooltip?

a da li bi trebali napraviti neki dobar interaktivni savremenog prikaza sa zadnjim tehnikama za prikaz i dinamicnost grafa graf koji prikazuje sve parametre koji ce ici po onom planu na graf, ppa da moze da se bira jeli prikaz temperatura i vlaga jeli, kisa, insolacija itd...
Balancing a modern interactive chart design against the MASTER_SPECIFICATION grouping and current backend data availability.

Odlično razmišljaš — baš po planu iz `MASTER_SPECIFICATION.md:6` treba 5 grupa grafika:

**1.** temperatura + vlaga (`T` + `H` — G1)
**2.** kiša (`RR` — G1)
**3.** vjetar (`BRV` prosjek + `PRV` smjer + `MUV` udar — G2)
**4.** pritisak (`P` — G3)
**5.** insolacija (`GR` — G3)

Backend već podržava sve (`?param=T`, `?param=H`, `?param=RR`, `?param=BRV`...), samo stranica trenutno prikazuje samo `T`.

**Kao profesionalac — da, napravićemo savremen interaktivni grafik gdje biraš grupu:**

* dugmići `T+H | Kiša | Vjetar | Pritisak | Insolacija`
* za `T+H` se crtaju **2 linije** (plava temp, zelena vlaga) na istom grafiku
* za `Vjetar` se crtaju 2-3 linije
* i dalje `24h | 48h | Sve` + tooltip

Hvala — vidim da zvanična prognoza radi, ali **tekst je zbrkan**:

* `danas` — ima `Jaki zemljotresi u CG...` (to je navigacija, ne prognoza)
* `Subota` — `05.09.2026. Za pomorce` (pomiješano)
* `Petak` — ima pravi tekst `U južnim i centralnim predjelima pretežno sunčano...` ✅ ali je pomiješan sa `Podgorica` i `prognoza ažurirana`

Znači naš čitač dijeli po riječi `Danas`/`Sjutra` svuda gdje je nađe, pa hvata i meni i navigaciju.

**Hajde da vidimo kako stvarno izgleda ta stranica da je popravimo:**

Nalijepi ovo:
```bash
curl -k -s "https://www.meteo.co.me/page.php?id=31" > /tmp/off.html
wc -l /tmp/off.html
grep -n "prognoza\|Prognoza\|Danas\|Sjutra" /tmp/off.html | head -20
grep -n "UpOZO\|pomor" /tmp/off.html | head -10
head -c 3000 /tmp/off.html | grep -a -o "<div[^>]*>.*prognoza.*" | head -c 600
echo ""
echo "---KRAJ OFF---"
```

Kopiraj mi **šta piše za `grep -n` i prvih par linija sa `prognoza`** — onda ću odmah popraviti `parseOfficial` da čita samo pravi tekst prognoze, ne i meni.

Odlična analiza — **potpuno se slažem, i to je tačno!**

To što je taj AI napisao je **100% ono što smo i mi vidjeli** kad smo `grep`-ovali:

* `prognoza-title` + `prognoza-text` + `prognoza-sign` + `cgprognoza-A.svg` za **danas** (`#tab_a`)
* Isto za **sjutra** (`#tab_b` + `cgprognoza-B.svg`)
* `Za pomorce` (`#tab_c` + `jjadran.svg`)

I ja sam upravo tako i popravio naš `parseOfficial.ts` u zadnjoj komandi — da čita baš te `prognoza-title/text/sign` blokove, a ne da traži riječ `Danas` svuda.

**Jedina mala razlika:** taj AI predlaže da idemo još preciznije po `id`-jevima `#tab_a`, `#tab_b`, `#tab_c` (po tabovima), što je **još stabilnije** nego moj regex koji traži sve `prognoza-title` redom. Mogu odmah da ga doradim da koristi baš `#tab_a/b/c` selektore — biće još čistije.

**I za ažuriranje:** tačno, ZHMS mijenja prognozu **3 puta dnevno** (i 2 puta za pomorce), pa ćemo i mi staviti cron na svakih **30-60 minuta** (kao što piše u `ARCHITECTURE.md:16` — svaki izvor ima svoj raspored, ne jedan za sve).

## 3. Parse (isti za svaku stanicu)

Jedan HTML = jedan dan jedne stanice jednog modela.

**Koraci:**

1. Učitaj HTML (cheerio / BS4).
2. Header: `Budva: 42.28 N, 18.80 E, wrf-nmm_e3km` → potvrda stanice + model.
3. Red sa datumom: `Četvrtak, 2026-09-03` → `weekday` + `date`.
4. `styleTn` → susjedni `style3b` = **Tmin**.
5. `styleTx` → susjedni `style3b` = **Tmax**.
6. Svaki data-red čiji prvi TD je `00|03|06|09|12|15|18|21`:
   - `utc`
   - `img[src*="Simbolcici"]` → `N/01` ili `D/03` (simbol)
   - RR: float, `-0.0` → `0`
   - RH: `"52."` → `52`
   - vjetar: `v1-045` → `wind_raw`, `wind_speed=1`, `wind_dir=45`

}

### Schema

```sql
CREATE TABLE numerical_days (
  id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  station TEXT NOT NULL,       -- BUD
  model TEXT NOT NULL,         -- a3km | e3km
  date TEXT NOT NULL,          -- YYYY-MM-DD
  weekday TEXT,
  tmin REAL,
  tmax REAL,
  elev_real REAL,
  elev_model REAL,

  UNIQUE(station, model, date)

CREATE TABLE numerical_slots (
  day_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES numerical_days(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  utc INTEGER NOT NULL,        -- 0..21 step 3
  symbol TEXT,
  rr REAL,
  rh INTEGER,
  wind_raw TEXT,
  wind_speed INTEGER,
  wind_dir INTEGER,
  PRIMARY KEY (day_id, utc)
);

CREATE INDEX idx_num_station_date ON numerical_days(station, date);
```

### Upsert strategija
- Po `(station, model, date)`: REPLACE / ON CONFLICT UPDATE.
- Slotovi: obriši stare za `day_id`, insert 8 novih (ili UPSERT po `(day_id, utc)`).

### API

```
GET /api/forecast/numerical?station=BUD&model=e3km
GET /api/forecast/numerical/BUD
GET /api/forecast/numerical?station=POD&model=a3km&days=5
GET /api/forecast/numerical/stations          # lista kodova + naziva

import type { StationCode } from "./stations";

export type NumericalModel = "a3km" | "e3km";

const BASE = "https://www.meteo.co.me/Meteorologija/Pr/Gradovi";

export function buildNumericalUrl(
  model: NumericalModel,
  station: StationCode | string,
  day: number
): string {
  if (day < 1 || day > 5) throw new Error(`day must be 1-5, got ${day}`);

  return `${BASE}/${folder}/${String(station).toUpperCase()}-${letter}${day}.html`;
}

AI je odgovorio:
Da ne kasniš više od **2–3 minuta** od trenutka kad se nešto pojavi na meteo.co.me, treba ti **kratki polling + pametni trigger**, ne jedan cron u 12:00.
---

## Princip

```
osvježenje na sajtu  →  max 2–3 min  →  ti imaš podatke u bazi/API
```

To znači: **poll na 60–90 s** u prozorima kad se očekuje update, a van toga rjeđe.

---

## Po tipu podataka

| Izvor | Ritam na sajtu | Kako da uhvatiš u ≤3 min |
|--------|----------------|---------------------------|
| **AWS hidro / meteo** (`aws_h.php`, `aws_m.php`) | ~satno (često :00–:05) | Poll **svakih 60–90 s** oko cijelog sata; van toga svakih 5 min |
| **SYNOP** (`synopT.php`) | termini ~07 / 14 / 21 h | Poll **svakih 60–90 s** od T−5 min do T+40 min |
| **Zvanična prognoza** (`page.php?id=31`) | ~3× dnevno (tekst) | Poll **svakih 2–3 min** u jutarnjem/poslijepodnevnom prozoru |
| **Numerička 5 dana** (HTML kartice) | ~2× dnevno (batch) | Poll **svakih 60–90 s** u prozorima 10:30–13:00 i 13:00–17:00 CEST |

Za tvoj cilj “nikad >3 min iza bilo čega” — najjednostavnije je:

> **Jedan worker koji svakih 90 s radi lagani check**, a full download samo kad se nešto promijeni.

---

## Konkretna strategija (preporučeno)

### 1. Sentinel (jeftin signal)

Ne skidaj 240 fajlova svake minute.

Za numeričku prognozu npr. samo:

```text
GET /Meteorologija/Pr/Gradovi/5danaE/BUD-E1.html
GET /Meteorologija/Pr/Gradovi/5danaA/BUD-A1.html
```

sa headerima:

```http
If-None-Match: "<zadnji-etag>"
If-Modified-Since: <zadnji-last-modified>
```

- **304** → ništa se nije mijenjalo → spavaj  
- **200** → batch je nov → odmah povuci **sve** stanice × 5 dana za taj model

Isto za:

- `aws_h.php` / `aws_m.php` — uporedi hash tijela ili `posljednje` timestamp  
- `synopT.php` — uporedi `sinopCGHour` + `sinopCGDay` ili hash niza  
- `page.php?id=31` — hash `.prognoza-text` + `.prognoza-sign`

### 2. Interval

```text
svakih 90 sekundi  →  sentinel check (1–4 requesta)
ako promjena      →  full fetch odmah
```

Kasniš najviše **~90 s**, u praksi često manje. To je unutar 2–3 min.

Ako hoćeš tvrdih ≤2 min: interval **60 s**.

### 3. Prošireni prozori (opciono, štedi requeste)

Ako ne želiš 24/7 na 90 s:

| Prozor (CEST) | Interval | Zašto |
|---------------|----------|--------|
| :55–:10 svakog sata | 60–90 s | AWS satni podaci |
| 06:30–09:00 | 60–90 s | SYNOP 07h + jutarnja prognoza |
| 10:30–13:00 | 60–90 s | numerička 00z batch |
| 13:00–16:30 | 60–90 s | numerička 12z + zvanična |
| 20:30–23:00 | 60–90 s | SYNOP 21h |
| ostalo | 3–5 min | rezervni catch-all |

I dalje ≤3 min u kritičnim periodima; van toga malo više, ali i dalje brzo.

Za “**uvijek** ≤2–3 min” → drži **90 s non-stop**.

---

## Minimalni worker (logika)

```
loop:
  for each source:
    r = conditional_get(sentinel_url)
    if r.status == 200:
      full_fetch(source)
      parse()
      upsert D1
      save new ETag / Last-Modified / content-hash
  sleep 90s
```

Timeouti kratki (5–10 s), retry 1×, concurrency 4–8 kad krene full fetch.

---

## Broj requesta (grub)

**Samo sentinel, 90 s non-stop:**

- ~4 requesta / 90 s ≈ **~3840 / dan** — sasvim prihvatljivo za njihov Apache

**Kad se numerička osvježi (2× dnevno):**

- + ~24 stanice × 5 dana × 1 model ≈ **120 requesta** po modelu  
- 2 modela × 2 runa ≈ **~480 ekstra / dan**

Ukupno red veličine **nekoliko hiljada requesta dnevno** — u redu ako imaš `User-Agent`, `Referer`, i throttle.

---

## Šta ne raditi

- Ne pollaj svih 240 HTML-ova svake minute  
- Ne oslanjaj se samo na cron u 12:00 i 15:00 — kasnićeš satima ako run zakasni  
- Ne ignoriši `304` / ETag — bez toga nepotrebno opterećuješ njih i sebe  

---

## Praktičan default za tebe

```text
Interval:        90 sekundi (non-stop)
Sentinel:        BUD-E1, BUD-A1, aws_h.php, synopT.php, page.php?id=31
Full fetch:      samo na promjenu
Cilj lag:        ≤ 90–120 s (sigurno unutar 2–3 min)
```

To je najjednostavniji način da **ne kasniš više od 2–3 minute** bez kompleksnog schedulinga i bez pretjeranog load-a na meteo.co.me.

---

## Koliko requesta generišeš

### Varijanta A — preporučena (sentinel 90 s + full samo na promjenu)

| Šta | Requesti / dan |
|-----|----------------|
| Sentinel non-stop (npr. 4 URL-a svakih 90 s) | ≈ 4 × 960 ≈ **3 800** |
| Full numerička (2 modela × ~2 runa × ~120 fajlova) | ≈ **400–500** |
| Full AWS / synop / zvanična (nekoliko × dnevno) | ≈ **50–150** |
| **Ukupno** | **≈ 4 500 – 5 000 / dan** |

To je:

- **~0.05 requesta u sekundi** prosječno  
- u peaku (kad krene full fetch) kratko **5–10 req/s** pa stane  

### Varijanta B — agresivnija (sve skidati svakih 90 s, bez ETag)

| Šta | Requesti / dan |
|-----|----------------|
| 240 numeričkih fajlova × 960 | ≈ **230 000** |
| + AWS + synop + page | još desetine hiljada |
| **Ukupno** | **stotine hiljada / dan** |

Ovo **jeste** pretjerano i može ih iznervirati ili automatski rate-limitovati.

---

## Koliko je to za njihov server

meteo.co.me je Apache javnog hidromet zavoda:

- Statički HTML + par PHP endpointa  
- Nema CDN-a, nema ogromnog capacity planninga  
- Ali **5 000 requesta dnevno** je ništa — to je nivo par desetina korisnika sa otvorenim tabom  

Za poređenje:

| Aktivnost | Red veličine |
|-----------|----------------|
| Jedan čovjek otvori stranicu i klikće | desetine–stotine req |
| Tvoj sentinel plan | ~5 000 / dan |
| Agresivan full-poll | 100 000+ / dan |
| Pravi DDoS / zlonamjeran scrape | milioni |

Zaključak: **Varijanta A je bezbjedna.** Varijanta B je nepristojna i nepotrebna.

---

## Rizik od ban-a IP

Realan rizik postoji uglavnom ako:

1. Radiš **stotina requesta u sekundi** duže vrijeme  
2. Nemaš normalan `User-Agent` / izgledaš kao bot-army  
3. Ignoirišeš `403` / `429` i nastavljaš juriš  
4. Skidaš cijeli sajt rekurzivno  

Sa tvojim planom (90 s, ETag, full samo na promjenu):

- **Rizik bana: vrlo nizak**  
- Izgledaš kao jedan stabilan monitoring klijent  

Ako ipak dobiješ `403` / `429`:

- odmah `sleep` 15–30 min  
- smanji frekvenciju  
- ne rotiraj proxyje da “zaobiđeš” — to je crvena zastava  

---

## Pravila da ostaneš “dobar građanin”

```text
1. Interval sentinel: 60–90 s (ne ispod 30 s)
2. Uvijek If-None-Match / If-Modified-Since
3. Full fetch samo kad sentinel kaže "promjena"
4. Full fetch: concurrency 4–8, ne 50 paralelno
5. Timeout 8–10 s, 1 retry max
6. User-Agent: jasan, npr.
   MontenegroWeatherBot/1.0 (+https://tvoj-sajt; kontakt@email)
7. Referer: https://www.meteo.co.me/
8. Poštuj 403/429 → backoff
9. Loguj broj requesta dnevno (da vidiš da nisi otišao u hiljade/min)
```

Opciono još bolje:

- noću (npr. 01–05 CEST) interval 3–5 min umjesto 90 s  
- ili samo prozori oko očekivanih update-a + sporiji catch-all  

---

## Brojke koje možeš držati kao limit

| Limit | Vrijednost | Komentar |
|-------|------------|----------|
| Prosjek | **< 0.2 req/s** | udobno |
| Kratki peak (full fetch) | **< 10 req/s**, < 30 s | OK |
| Dnevni budget | **< 10 000 req/dan** | još uvijek blago |
| Alarm | **> 50 000 / dan** ili stalni 403 | smanji odmah |

Tvoj plan (~5k/dan) je **na ~pola** od konzervativnog “udobnog” limita.

---

## Finalna preporuka

Radi ovako:

- **90 s sentinel** (4–5 URL-ova)  
- **full samo na promjenu**  
- concurrency mala, ETag, jasan UA  

Opterećenje: **zanemarljivo**.  
Rizik bana: **praktično nula**, dok god ne pretvoriš to u full scrape svake minute.
